chapter: Road bands and the Gillespie band
title: Gillespie band personnel and the Afro-Cuban repertoire
summary: He names the sidemen and writers in the band and the Afro-Cuban pieces still played after Chano Pozo's death.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Who were some of the other people in the, in the orchestra at that time?
Oh there was uh Joe Gayles, the other tenor player, Ernie Henry...

...the third alto player, John Brown, first [alto saxophone]. Um...uh there was [James] “Hen Gates” [Forman] on piano, Willie Kirk on trumpet. Um...Al McKibbon on Tape 1, 33:09-35:26 bass, [Louis] “Sabu” Martinez, conga drum. Um...Lamar Brothers[?] on trumpet, uh J.J. Johnson on trombone, Sam Most, trombone.
Andy [Duryea]...I can’t think of Andy’s last name on trombone. It was a dynamic band, and, of course, the people who were writing for the band, John Lewis....um and other prominent writers.
So, were some of the–you mentioned Sabu Martinez–were a lot of the Afro- Cuban pieces still being played by the orchestra at this time?
Yeah, that was the time, yeah. Of course, [Luciano] “Chano” Pozo [Gonzales] had just departed.
Passed, but they were still playing those tinged compositions: Cubana Be, Cubana Bop.
